docs.title: GregTech Terminals
docs.text: A lightweight GregTech CEu Modern addon. It adds four Terminals that inspect and manipulate GTM multiblocks, plus a public API for mods and KubeJS packs to register their own tiered components.

docs.title: Terminals
docs.text:
• Multi-Structure Manager: sees every multiblock within a 32-block radius and upgrades any tiered block (coils, I/O hatches, I/O buses, energy hatches, parallel hatches, mufflers, custom tiered casings) straight from your inventory or AE2. It can also auto-build a structure and request missing blocks from your ME network.
  • Schematic Interface: shift + right-click a controller to copy a formed structure as a named schematic, then paste it later (optionally pulling blocks from AE2).
  • Dismantler: shift + right-click a controller to pick up every block of the structure into your inventory.
  • Energy Analyzer: Monitor the energy usage of machines, multiblocks, energy hatches, singleblocks and battery boxes.

docs.title: For pack and mod developers
docs.text:
Terminals can recognize and upgrade blocks from other mods. Register them through either surface:

  • Registering Components (Java): the full TerminalAPI, every component category, custom groups and detectors.
  • Registering Components (KubeJS): the GTCEuTerminalEvents.components startup event for packs.
  • Tier Reference: the shared tier number to voltage name table used by both.

docs.title: Supported mods and packs
docs.text:
Specially tailored integrations for unique hatches and tiered casings:

  • AstroGreg: Exsilium
  • TerraFirmaGreg
  • Phoenix Forge Technologies
  • GTM Things
  • Star Technology: Beyond

Report pack-specific bugs on the issue tracker or on Discord. To request an integration, leave a suggestion.

docs.title: Dismantler
docs.text:
The Dismantler removes a formed multiblock in one click.

Shift + right-click a multiblock controller to pick up every block that is part of the structure and place it in your inventory. If your inventory is full, any excess blocks are dropped on the ground.

docs.title: Energy Analyzer
docs.text:
The Energy Analyzer records and monitors the energy usage of your multiblocks.

It can link:

  • Multiblocks
  • I/O energy hatches
  • Singleblock machines
  • Battery boxes

docs.title: Multi-Structure Manager
docs.text: The Multi-Structure Manager (MSM) scans for every multiblock within a 32-block radius of the player and lets you inspect, upgrade, and auto-build structures without making them hand by hand.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
• Scan: detects multiblocks nearby and lists their components grouped by category.
  • Upgrade: swaps any tiered block in place (coils, energy hatches, I/O hatches and buses, parallel hatches, mufflers, custom tiered casings) using blocks from your inventory or your ME network.
  • Auto-build: builds the full structure for a controller, placing blocks from your inventory or AE2 and requesting what is missing.
  • Request: queues missing blocks as AE2 crafting.

docs.title: AE2 link
docs.text: The Manager connects to your ME network through a Wireless Access Point. Link it while in range of an access point, then turn on Use AE2 in the settings to pull upgrade and build materials from the network.

docs.title: Auto-build settings
docs.text:
Open the settings panel to control how the Manager builds a structure.

Setting Values What it does No Hatch Mode Yes / No Build the structure without placing hatches, buses or other multiblock parts (casings only). Tier Preference 0 to 14 The exact tier to use for tiered blocks. If that tier is not available, the nearest tier you have is used. Repeat Count 0 to 99 How many times to repeat a repeatable layer. 0 uses the structure minimum. Use AE2 Yes / No Pull, build and upgrade materials from the linked ME network. Requires an access point link.

docs.title: How Tier Preference works
docs.text:
Tier Preference is a priority filter, for any cell that accepts a tiered block, the Manager prefers the block whose tier matches your number exactly. If you do not have that tier (in your inventory or ME network), it fallbacks to the nearest tier you do have.

Example: set Tier Preference to 4 (EV).

  • You have an EV energy hatch: it places EV.
  • You only have an IV hatch: it places IV.
  • You have both IV and UHV: it places IV, because IV is closer to EV than UHV.

This works for every tiered block the same way, including custom components registered by other mods. See Registering Components (Java) and Registering Components (KubeJS).

docs.title: Registering Components (Java)
docs.text:
Use TerminalAPI to expose existing blocks to Terminals so it can recognize, display, and offer them as upgrade candidates.

Call these methods inside FMLCommonSetupEvent:

import com.gtceuterminal.api.TerminalAPI;
import com.gtceuterminal.common.config.ComponentEntry;
import com.gtceuterminal.common.config.ComponentRegistry;
import com.gtceuterminal.common.multiblock.ComponentGroup;

@Mod.EventBusSubscriber(modid = MODID, bus = Mod.EventBusSubscriber.Bus.MOD)
public class MyModEvents {

    @SubscribeEvent
    public static void commonSetup(FMLCommonSetupEvent event) {
        event.enqueueWork(() -> {
            TerminalAPI.registerCoil(...);
            TerminalAPI.registerEnergyHatch(...);
            // etc.
        });
    }
}

docs.title: Coils
docs.text:
TerminalAPI.registerCoil(
    "mymod:graphene_coil",  // block registry ID
    "Graphene Coil",        // display name
    8,                      // tier, see Tier Reference
    9600                    // temperature in K
);

docs.title: Generic Component
docs.text:
For blocks that do not fit any standard category, or when you need extra attributes:

TerminalAPI.registerComponent(
    ComponentRegistry.ENERGY_HATCHES,   // or any custom String category
    ComponentEntry.builder("mymod:special_hatch", "Special Hatch", "UEV", 9)
        .attr("hatchType", "INPUT")
        .attr("amperage", "64A")
        .build()
);

Built-in category constants on ComponentRegistry:

Constant String value ENERGY_HATCHES "energy_hatches" FLUID_HATCHES "fluid_hatches" BUSES "buses" LASER_HATCHES "laser_hatches" WIRELESS_HATCHES "wireless_hatches" SUBSTATION_HATCHES "substation_hatches" PARALLEL_HATCHES "parallel_hatches" MUFFLER_HATCHES "muffler_hatches" MAINTENANCE_HATCHES "maintenance_hatches" DUAL_HATCHES "dual_hatches" COILS "coils"

docs.title: Custom Groups
docs.text:
Use this when your mod/addon introduces a PartAbility. The detector lambda enables automatic detection during multiblock scanning. Without it blocks only appear in Terminals if registered manually via TerminalAPI.registerComponent().

TerminalAPI.registerGroup(
    ComponentGroup.builder("my_hatch", "My Hatch")
        .color(0xFF00AAFF)
        .energyHandler()
        .registryCategory(ComponentRegistry.WIRELESS_HATCHES)
        .detector(b -> MyAddon.MY_ABILITY.isApplicable(b))
        .build(),
    "my_ability_name"   // PartAbility.getname()
);

docs.title: Registering Components (KubeJS)
docs.text:
GTCEu Terminals exposes a startup event for registering existing blocks into Terminals. Scripts go in kubejs/startup_scripts/.

GTCEuTerminalEvents.components(event => {
    // register things here
});

docs.title: What this event does
docs.text:
This event registers existing blocks so Terminals knows about them. It tells Terminals how to classify, display, and upgrade a block that already exists in the game.

It does not create new blocks. KubeJS cannot create hatch part machines because GTM does not expose MultiblockPartMachine, IO, or EnergyHatchPartMachine as KubeJS bindings so creating a new hatch requires Java.

What this event is for:

  • A mod/addon already created a hatch block and registered it with a GTM PartAbility.
  • You want Terminals to recognize it so show it in the component list, and offer it as an upgrade candidate.

Automatic detection works for any block registered under a standard GTM PartAbility (INPUT_ENERGY, IMPORT_FLUIDS, INPUT_LASER, etc.). Terminals scans the multiblock and component groups automatically. In that case this event is only needed to populate the upgrade candidate list with the correct metadata.

For blocks using a custom PartAbility from another addon, automatic detection requires a Java detector lambda. See Registering Components (Java).

docs.title: Generic Component
docs.text:
Registers a block into any category without needing a specific method. Useful for blocks that do not fit a standard type, or when you need extra attributes.

event.addComponent(
    "energy_hatches",
    "mymod:uev_64a_energy_hatch",  // block registry ID, must already exist
    "UEV 64A Energy Hatch",
    9,
    {hatchType: "INPUT", amperage: "64A"}  // optional attrs map
);

// Without attrs
event.addComponent("coils", "mymod:graphene_coil", "Graphene Coil", 8);

docs.title: Custom Groups
docs.text:
Registers a new component group. In Java, pairing a group with a detector lambda makes its blocks show up as their own category in the detail and upgrade panels during multiblock scanning.

From KubeJS you cannot pass a detector, so a group created here will not form a scanned category on its own. Use it to give the blocks you add with addComponent a home and the correct upgrade metadata; for a group that is detected automatically, create it in Java with a detector (see Registering Components (Java)).

// 1. Register the group
event.addGroup(
    "my_custom_hatch",   // unique id
    "My Custom Hatch",   // display name
    0xFF00AAFF,          // color as 0xAARRGGBB
    "energy",            // handlerType: "energy", "fluid", "item", "data", "special", or null
    "energy_hatches",    // registryCategory, where upgrade candidates are looked up
    true                 // upgradeable
);

// 2. Register the blocks into that category so they appear as upgrade candidates
event.addComponent("energy_hatches", "mymod:my_hatch_input", "My Input Hatch", 9, {hatchType: "INPUT"});
event.addComponent("energy_hatches", "mymod:my_hatch_output", "My Output Hatch", 9, {hatchType: "OUTPUT"});

handlerType controls which section of the UI the group appears in:

Value Section "energy" Energy handlers "fluid" Fluid handlers "item" Item handlers "data" Data handlers "special" Special components (maintenance, muffler, etc.) null Generic / uncategorized

Note: Only "energy" and "data" currently change behavior (they control which groups the Energy Analyzer inspects). "fluid", "item", and "special" are accepted and stored, but nothing reads them yet, so they have no functional effect today. Set them so the metadata is correct for the future, but do not rely on them changing anything for now.

docs.title: Schematic Interface
docs.text: The Schematic Interface copies and pastes multiblock structures.

docs.title: Copy
docs.text: Shift + right-click a multiblock controller to copy every block that is part of the structure and save it as a named schematic for easy pasting later.

docs.title: Paste
docs.text: Paste a saved schematic. The interface can connect to your ME network to pull the blocks it needs.

docs.title: Blueprint (Planned)
docs.text: Being able to save builds/lines, is a planned feature and is not complete yet

docs.title: Requesting (planned)
docs.text: Requesting blocks that are not in your inventory or network is a planned feature and is not complete yet.

docs.title: Tier Reference
docs.text:
Tiers are passed as integers throughout the API and the Multi-Structure Manager. This is the mapping from tier number to GregTech voltage name.

Tier Name 0 ULV 1 LV 2 MV 3 HV 4 EV 5 IV 6 LuV 7 ZPM 8 UV 9 UHV 10 UEV 11 UIV 12 UXV 13 OpV 14 MAX

See also: Registering Components (Java), Registering Components (KubeJS), Multi-Structure Manager.
